extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent classifiers, and patent practitioners (agents/attorneys) who use the CPC
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for classifying patent documents into CPC sections and subclasses (notes for sections A–Y). Explains classifying characteristics, definitions, exceptions, and where to place features (e.g. separation processes, chemical aspects, engines, electrical aspects, tagging).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation classification characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: The classifying characteristics for separation subclasses are: (1) the physical state of the matter to be separated, (2) the principle of the process used, and (3) particular kinds of apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three characteristics are used to decide among subclasses (e.g. B01D, B03B, B03C, B03D, B04B, B04C, B07B, B07C). The physical-state characteristic is further broken into liquid/liquid or liquid/gas and gas/gas; solid/liquid or solid/gas; solid/solid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical-state grouping for separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical-state classification is assembled in three groups: (a) liquid/liquid, liquid/gas, gas/gas; (b) solid/liquid, solid/gas; (c) solid/solid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these groups as the first aspect when deciding which subclass to apply; subsequent choice is by principle and apparatus. The guide explicitly enumerates these three groups (labels a, b, c).

rubrics_metrics.name: B01D as the general class for separations (non solid/solid)
rubrics_metrics.description: B01D is the most general class for separation other than solids-from-solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When separation does not involve solids-from-solids, B01D should generally be used for operations and methods; apparatus aspects may point to B01D as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use B03B vs B07B for solids-from-solids
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparatus for separating solids from solids are covered by B03B when the process is regarded as the equivalent of 'washing' (mining sense), even if pneumatic; screens per se are not in B03B but in B07B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a solids-from-solids apparatus functions like a washing process (e.g. pneumatic tables or jigs) classify in B03B; screens per se go to B07B; other dry-method apparatus for solids-from-solids go to B07B.

rubrics_metrics.name: B07C for detection/measurement-based sorting
rubrics_metrics.description: If the separation takes place as a result of the detection or measurement of some feature of the material or articles to be sorted it is classified in B07C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use B07C for individual sorting or classification methods that rely on sensing/measuring properties (optical, weight, dimension, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Isotope separation classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The separation of isotopes of the same chemical element is covered by B01D 59/00, whatever process or apparatus is employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isotope-separation inventions go to the dedicated place in B01D regardless of whether they use centrifuges, chemical exchange, membranes, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method–subclass mappings for liquid/gas separations
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide maps methods and apparatus to subclasses: general operations/methods for liquid/liquid, liquid/gas, gas/gas go to B01D; by centrifugal force (centrifuges/free-vortex) to B01D (operations) and B04B/B04C (apparatus); using magnetic or electrostatic effects to B03C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying, consult the method–apparatus table: e.g. centrifuge methods may be cross-referenced to B04B/B04C as apparatus; electrostatic or magnetic separation points to B03C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method–subclass mappings for solid/liquid separations
rubrics_metrics.description: For solid/liquid (or solid/gas) separations: general operations/methods are in B01D; centrifugal methods and centrifuge apparatus map to B01D and B04B/B04C respectively; magnetic/electrostatic effects map to B03C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same mapping logic as liquid separations: first decide operation class (B01D), then apparatus may point to B04B/B04C or B03C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid/solid dry-methods classification mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Dry-method solids/solids: general bulk methods, screening/sifting, pneumatic sorting and centrifugal force map to B07B; individual sorting maps to B07C; pneumatic tables or jigs correspond to B03B; magnetic/electrostatic effects map to B03C; centrifuges/free-vortex apparatus may map to B04B/B04C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between bulk processes (B07B) and individual sorting (B07C); apparatus that imitate 'washing' (pneumatic tables/jigs) go to B03B even if pneumatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid/solid wet-methods classification mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Wet-method solids/solids: general wet methods map to B03B; flotation/differential sedimentation map to B03D; screening may still be in B07B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combinations (dry+wet) are treated as B03B. Use the wet-method mapping when a liquid medium is essential to the separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of chemical-element groups (section C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section C defines groups of elements for classification: e.g. ALKALI METALS (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr), ALKALINE EARTH METALS, LANTHANIDES, RARE EARTHS, ACTINIDES, REFRACTORY METALS, HALOGENS, NOBLE GASES, PLATINUM GROUP, NOBLE METALS, LIGHT METALS, HEAVY METALS, IRON GROUP, NON-METALS, METALS, TRANSITION ELEMENTS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these standard lists when classifying chemical inventions to determine subgroup membership and related indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Section C (chemistry; metallurgy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section C covers pure chemistry (inorganic, organic, macromolecular compounds and methods of preparation), applied chemistry (compositions like glass, ceramics, fertilisers, plastics, paints, petroleum products), certain marginal industries (coke manufacture, fuels, oils/fats, fermentation, sugar), certain operations or treatments, and metallurgy (ferrous or non-ferrous alloys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject-matter has a dominant chemical aspect, classify in Section C; the section is intended to keep chemically similar matters together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule: chemical part/aspect covered by Section C when mixed aspects exist
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of operations, treatments, products, or articles having both a chemical and non-chemical part or aspect, the general rule is that the chemical part or aspect is covered by Section C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inventions have intertwined chemical and mechanical aspects, prefer Section C for the chemical aspect unless a note or reference indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions where non-chemical aspect carries classification
rubrics_metrics.description: There are exceptions where the mechanical (or non-chemical) aspect carries with it the chemical aspect and is classified elsewhere: e.g. extractive processes in A61K; chemical purification of air in A61L; chemical firefighting in A62D; chemical processes and apparatus in B01; impregnation of wood in B27K; chemical methods of analysis/testing in G01N; photographic materials/processes in G03; treatment of textiles and production of paper in Section D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these exception examples when the mechanical/application context makes another section more appropriate despite chemical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocked chemical/mechanical aspects may lead to split coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: When the chemical and mechanical aspects are so closely interlocked that a neat division is not possible, Section C may cover the chemical aspect and a part only of the mechanical aspect (e.g. after-treatments of artificial stone in C04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for notes or references to clarify boundaries; the guide may give an explicit cross-reference when coverage is partial or arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where chemical is in C but applied use elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes the pure chemical aspect is in Section C while the applied chemical aspect is classified in another section because of the use (e.g. treatment of plants/animals in A01N; foodstuffs in A23; munitions/explosives in F42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify according to the intended use: if the invention is primarily a use (e.g. for food or animals), prefer the target-use section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of key terms for subsection F (engines/pumps/machines)
rubrics_metrics.description: In subsection F, key terms have precise meanings: 'engine' = device continuously converting fluid energy into mechanical power (excluding single-stroke devices); 'pump' = device continuously raising/forcing/compressing/exhausting fluid; 'machine' = device which could equally be an engine and a pump; 'positive displacement' and 'non-positive displacement' have specific operational meanings; 'oscillating-piston machine', 'rotary-piston machine', 'rotary piston', 'co-operating members', 'movement of co-operating members', 'teeth or tooth-equivalents', 'internal-axis type', 'free-piston', 'cylinders', 'main shaft', 'plant', 'working fluid', 'steam' and 'special vapour', 'reaction type' and 'impulse type' are all defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these precise definitions when deciding subclass placement in F01–F04; the definitions affect whether an apparatus is treated as an engine, pump, or machine and which subclass applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule: subclasses designating 'engines' or 'pumps' cover methods of operating them
rubrics_metrics.description: In subsection F, subclasses or groups designating 'engines' or 'pumps' cover methods of operating the same unless otherwise specifically provided for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an invention concerns operating methods of engines/pumps, classify in the engine/pump-designated subclass unless a special provision states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of accessories of machines/engines (valves, lubricating, silencers, cooling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclically operating valves, lubricating gear, gas-flow silencers, exhaust apparatus, or cooling should be classified in subclasses F01L, F01M, F01N, F01P irrespective of stated application, unless their classifying features are peculiar to their application (then classify in the relevant subclass of F01–F04). Lubricating/gas-flow silencers/exhaust or cooling of machines/engines should be in F01M/F01N/F01P except those peculiar to steam engines (F01B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally classify auxiliary apparatus in the listed subclasses; only move them where the accessory's classifying features are peculiar to a specific application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal classifying characteristics in F: genus, principle, complementarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal classifying characteristic of subclasses in F is the genus of apparatus (machines; engines; pumps). These genera are further subdivided by principle of operation (positive/non-positive displacement) and by kind of apparatus (simple reciprocating piston; rotary or oscillating piston; other). Another characteristic is the working fluid (liquid and elastic fluid; elastic fluid; liquid). Complementarity associates pairs of subclasses according to these characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided complementarity table to find corresponding subclasses (e.g. relations among F01B, F03B, F04B, F03C, etc.). Consider genus first, then operation principle, then kind of apparatus and working fluid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition note: 'variable' and classification difficulty in G
rubrics_metrics.description: In Section G, 'variable' is defined as a measurable feature or property of an entity. Classification in this Section may be difficult because distinctions often rest on the user's intention rather than constructional differences, and many subjects are systems/combinations sharing common features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the real nature of the invention (including intended purpose) before classifying; consult class-specific definitions (e.g. 'measuring' in G01, 'control' in G05). Examples in the guide show how the same device may fall into different subclasses depending on purpose (display for education vs advertising vs measurement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule: electrical aspects classification (Section H general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, any electric aspect or part peculiar to a particular operation/process/apparatus/object/article classified in another section is classified in the subclass for that subject rather than in H; the basic-electricity aspect (basic elements, circuits) appears in Section H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the electrical aspect is incidental to a device primarily covered by another section, classify the electrical part with that section unless common electrical characteristics at class level suggest H; examples given include therapeutic apparatus (A61), laboratory/industrial electric processes (B01), electricity supply in transport sections, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special cases splitting electrical vs mechanical aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: There are special cases where mechanical arrangement vs electrical elements are split between sections: e.g. electric heating generally covered by F24D/F24H/F27 while electrical aspect in H05B; electric lighting mechanical arrangement in F21V while elements and primary circuits are in H; electric furnaces considered in H; welding circuits are B23K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an invention combines electrical elements with a mechanical arrangement, decide whether classification should follow the electrical aspect (H or H05B) or the mechanical arrangement (F21V, etc.) according to the guide's examples and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Section Y tagging classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Classes Y02 and Y04 are only to be used for tagging documents which are already classified or indexed elsewhere and which relate in a broad sense to specific major technical fields; primary purpose is to monitor new technological development and tag cross-sectional technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tagging codes in Section Y do not replace the main classification codes of other sections. Y10 was introduced to accommodate subjects formerly in USPC cross-reference art collections (XRACs) and digests.
